top3.why: AJJ (formerly Andrew Jackson Jihad) bring their scrappy, politically sharp folk-punk to Philly on the Dirty Old Power tour, with Greet Death opening. It's an all-ages R5 Productions show at First Unitarian — Philly's home base for exactly this kind of DIY, community-minded bill. Doors at 7:30, show at 8; tickets run about $33.

Palestine Cinema Days' touring program brings the documentary "Foragers" to Vox Populi — a rare chance to see Palestinian and Palestine-focused nonfiction film on a big screen here, outside the festival circuit. Vox Populi is an artist-run cooperative gallery, a few blocks from the Convention Center and the Market-Frankford Line's 11th Street stop.

PhilaMOCA's long-running Psychotronic Film Society pulls another deep-cut genre oddity out of the vault — cheap ($5 at the door), weird, and exactly what this venue exists for. Doors at 7, screening at 7:30; the series doesn't always name the film in advance, which is part of the appeal.

annotations.note: Cookbook authors Leah Koenig and Susan Spungen talk Jewish desserts, paired with a tasting from The Dessert Table and The Cookie Queen.
Ongoing reading group working through Ursula K. Le Guin's The Dispossessed — her anarchist-utopia novel, a direct hit for anyone into leftist political fiction.
Fire Museum Presents: experimental duo Ak'chamel and Ecology, now sold out.
Online meetup watch-along for A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors (1987).
Guided tour of the Art Museum's Marcel Duchamp exhibition; runs multiple days this week.
Guided tour through the museum's Titian to Turner collection; runs multiple days this week.

top3.why: PhilaMOCA marks Godzilla Day with a 16mm screening of "Godzilla vs. the Smog Monster," plus trailers, shorts, and a promised special guest kaiju. It's the kind of gleefully specific, print-format programming that makes this the city's best home for genre film. Doors at 7, screening at 7:30.

Hovvdy bring their warm, unhurried indie-folk to First Unitarian on their Big World Tour, with Christian Lee Hutson opening — another all-ages R5 bill at Philly's most storied all-ages room. Doors 7:30, show 8; tickets around $31.

An unusual two-piano bill: contemporary-classical pianist/composer Timo Andres paired with jazz pianist Aaron Diehl at the Perelman Theater. Diehl is one of the more interesting jazz pianists working today, and this crossover pairing is a genuinely distinctive program for a Tuesday night in Center City.

annotations.note: Silent co-working session for writers at Iffy Books — three 40-minute writing blocks with breaks, BYO coffee.
Election night community gathering at Headlong Dance Theater; details are thin on Do215, so confirm specifics before heading over. *(confirm details)*
Palace (Willie J. Healey opening, per WXPN) at Franklin Music Hall.
Free outdoor jazz series at FDR Park, South Philly.
Viewing party for The Boulet Brothers' Dragula season 7 premiere at Strangelove's, in the Gayborhood.
Community guitar skill-share at The Velvet Whip.
Experimental improvisation session built around Taal Baladi (Arabic rhythmic patterns).
Online meetup watch-along for Nightmare on Elm Street 4 and 5.

top3.why: Peter Greenaway's grotesque, operatic 1989 classic gets a rare theatrical outing at PFS's Film Society Center — gorgeous, violent, and about as far from a typical multiplex Wednesday as repertory film gets. Rated R, 1 hr 55 min.

The National Lawyers Guild runs a Know Your Rights and Risks training at Wooden Shoe Books — practical, timely legal-rights education for protest, direct action, and organizing, hosted at Philly's longest-running anarchist bookshop. No cost is listed; confirm admission when you arrive.

Iffy Books opens its gear up for an afternoon of VHS and audio-cassette experimentation — bring tapes, learn analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog transfer, and tinker with hardware most people threw out years ago. Exactly the hands-on DIY-electronics programming this space is known for.

annotations.note: A Nash the Slash tribute/revival night at PhilaMOCA — the masked, bandaged avant-garde musician's cult following keeps this kind of programming alive. $12 at the door.
Marxist Reading Group works through Bukharin's The ABCs of Communism at People's Headquarters.
Panel on lesbian artists across the decades with Sinister Wisdom, featuring exhibiting artists KT Abadir-Mullally, Ira Balachanthiran and Morgan Gwenwald.
The Rotunda's standing Wednesday drop-in improvised-music jam.
Jazz flutist Elena Pinderhughes at City Winery.
Jazz vocalist Jackie Johnson and her ensemble at Chris' Jazz Cafe.
Latin jazz jam session at Black Squirrel Club.
Expert panel on medical AI at the Mütter Museum.
DC215 AppSec Village session on reverse-engineering and patching legacy software. Online.
Talk on Reconstruction and the Second Founding at the National Constitution Center.
Online meetup watch-along for Freddy's Dead: The Final Nightmare and Wes Craven's New Nightmare.

top3.why: Iffy Books hosts a beginner-friendly introduction to Strudel, a live-coding tool for making music with code, ending in a group livecode jam. No programming experience required — DIY electronics, functional-style programming, and music overlapping in exactly the way this space does best.

PhilaMOCA stacks Oldest Sea with three more local acts — Bruise Bath, ShyGodwin, and Diuretic — for $15, an all-local, multi-band bill that's easy to miss outside this venue's own listings. Doors 7, show 7:30.

Experimental composer Lea Bertucci (paired with Michael Behari as Bow and Arrow) splits a bill with the duo Angel Meat at The Perch in Kensington — a small-room experimental/noise show that's easy to miss. Bertucci's work spans tape loops, saxophone, and site-specific sound installation; expect something more textural than a standard rock bill. A quick ride up the Market-Frankford Line into Kensington.

annotations.note: Jazz saxophonist Kamasi Washington co-headlines with Ami Taf Ra at City Winery — no showtime listed; check the venue site before heading over.
This Is Lorelei (WXPN Welcomes, an R5 all-ages show) at First Unitarian.
Beginner soldering workshop: build a 3.5mm audio aux cable with a volume knob.
Imperial Teen, Kristeen Young, and Gay Meat — indie/punk triple bill.
Fruit Bats, with Sarah Klang opening (per WXPN), at Union Transfer.
HFB Ensemble at Chris' Jazz Cafe.
Erini — Fos: An Asia Minor Story, at The Rotunda.
The Moth's Philadelphia GrandSLAM storytelling competition at Bok Building.
Slum Village & Pete Rock at Brooklyn Bowl.
Renters United Philadelphia's monthly tenant-organizing meeting, over Zoom.
"Jewish or Antisemitic LIVE," hosted by Eitan Levine, at the Weitzman museum.
Oscar Wilde: Shadows Beneath the Spotlight, at the Rosenbach — now sold out.
Preview Party kicking off the Art Museum's 50th Annual Craft Show, which runs through the weekend.

top3.why: Homies Helping Homies' South Philly garage space hosts a benefit show in support of SPAC, stacked with a metal/punk/screamo bill — the kind of DIY, all-local, community-funding lineup that only shows up on punk-specific listings like Ask a Punk. All-ages, basement-show energy, minutes from Point Breeze.

Johnny Brenda's goes goth for A Black Celebration, a dark-music DJ night from Phillygoth.net with DJs Baby Berlin and Alex English. 21+, 9pm–2am, $10 advance / $15 at the door — a straightforward match for anyone into gothic club culture. In Fishtown; nearest stop is Girard on the Market-Frankford Line, or the 15 trolley.
The Philly Pigeon's Late(ish) Poetry Show brings spoken word to PhilaMOCA's screen-and-stage room — $15–25 for a small, text-forward night at a venue better known for film. Doors 8, show 8:30.

annotations.note: Philly 2600's monthly meetup for local hackers, phreaks, and infosec folks, at Iffy Books.
Basia Bulat, seated solo show at Philadelphia Ethical Society. $37.
The Tenor Madness Septet, with saxophonists Eric Alexander and Victor North, at Chris' Jazz Cafe — a later set with trombonist Conrad Herwig follows.
Miki Yamanaka Trio, part of a First Friday jazz/PAAFF collaboration at the Barnes Foundation.
"Sex & Death"-themed drag/performance night at Prism Arts Philadelphia.
Open studio and exhibition for Dunu's artists-in-residence at Termite TV Studio, Cherry Street Pier.
First Friday opening at Arch Enemy Arts, the city's go-to gallery for dark and pop-surrealist work.
First Friday double opening at Paradigm Gallery: André Schulze's "Restored and Reimagined" and Kyle Montgomery's "LUX."
Completely Yes plays the music of Stevie Wonder at Woodmere Art Museum.
Online meetup watch-along for Godzilla Minus One, ahead of the sequel's theatrical run.

top3.why: William Basinski brings "The Disintegration Loops" — his landmark, elegiac ambient work built from tape loops literally dissolving as they played, recorded in the days around 9/11 — to a seated 25th-anniversary performance in First Unitarian's sanctuary, with claire rousay opening. About as rare and significant as an experimental-music booking gets in Philadelphia. Doors 7:30, show 8.

The Rotunda's second annual Modular Synth Fest gathers five local electronic/experimental artists — Kevin Dal-Mare, David Taliento, Jair-Rohm Parker Wells, Kwame Johnson, and Sandy James — for an afternoon built entirely around hardware synthesis. The DIY-electronics-meets-music crossover this space exists for, and a real rarity on the Philly calendar.

Sanctuary in West Philly hosts a crust/hardcore punk bill headlined by out-of-town act Housie (rva), with Sediment and Insectoids — the kind of DIY show that lives entirely on Ask a Punk's radar and nowhere else.

annotations.note: Gandahar (1987), René Laloux's hallucinatory French animated sci-fi cult classic, at PFS Film Society Center.
Sex Dwarf: Notorious November, a goth/industrial dance night hosted by WXPN's own Robert Drake, at Broad Hall. 21+, $5 before 9pm.
Smoke (1995) at PFS Film Society Center.
Ghost Harmonics: an experimental bill at The Perch featuring poet Bianca Stone alongside BORBS, World Assembly Body Opera, and others.
Giles Corey (Dan Barrett's dark-ambient project) with Kathryn Mohr and Val Acton Loper, at Ukie Club.
Frankenstein pop-up exhibit at the Mütter Museum — included with admission; has been running weekly since September.
August Lamm's "You Don't Need a Smartphone" book tour stop at Studio 34.
Build a pocket digital notebook with a USB keyboard, at Iffy Books.
Sloptart, Smellco, and Annalakka at Silk City.
Claude Code Philly's weekly hands-on meetup for builders using Claude to write code. Online.

top3.why: Deerhoof — one of indie rock's most genuinely singular, long-running experimental bands — hits Underground Arts with Eraser and Nympho opening. Twenty-plus years in, they still don't sound like anyone else; a rare chance to see a true original in a room this size.

A five-band punk and metal matinee at Nikki Lopez — Trash Strike, XPURITYX, Rights Abuse, Drawn By Blood, and False Nine — starting at 1pm, the kind of all-day DIY bill that's easy to miss if you're not specifically looking for it.

top3.address: 101 S Independence Mall East, Philadelphia, PA 19106
top3.why: Secret Chord Concerts pairs an Ethiofunk set from Gili Yalo with a Sigd celebration — the Ethiopian Jewish holiday marking renewal of the covenant — at the Weitzman museum. A genuinely rare pairing of live world music and a specific cultural observance you won't find anywhere else in the city this week.

annotations.note: Bowerbird presents Postal Pieces 3, an experimental/new-music program, at The Perch.
Black Squirrel Noir: alternative, new wave, and goth DJ night with Kathy Fadigan, Jon Gill, and EGBIII. $10 advance / $15 at the door.
Screening of Nuevo mundo (1978) paired with a workshop on ancestral connection and syncretism, at The Rotunda.
Anarchist Sewing Club — learn to sew or mend clothes, or just hang out sewing, at Iffy Books.
IndieWeb Homebrew Website Club, part of a worldwide network reclaiming the web from social media, at Iffy Books.
Barnes Cinema screens Powwow People, Sky Hopinka's documentary, at the Barnes Foundation.
Philly DSA's New Member 101 orientation session.
Wavy Movy Fundraising Festival at The Perch.
Weekly online watch party for Dexter: Resurrection, Season 2.
Curtis Symphony Orchestra, Yannick Nézet-Séguin conducting Mahler's Ninth, at Marian Anderson Hall.
